newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asahi Chemical to shut polystyrene plant - paper.
newsitem.headline: Asahi Chemical to shut polystyrene plant - paper.

text.p: Asahi Chemical Industry Co will close a polystyrene production facility at its Kawasaki plant, near Tokyo, this month, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Wednesday.
The paper said Asahi is placing an emphasis on overseas markets and the shutdown is aimed at relieving overcapacity in the market.
It will be the first time a petrochemical production facility has been shut in Japan since 1983, the paper said.
The facility is the oldest of its kind in Japan and has an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes of the major synthetic resin, the paper said.
A spokesman for Asahi Chemical was not immediately available to comment on the report.
Asahi Chemical said in February that it and Dow Chemical Co of the United States plan to set up a joint venture in China to produce polystyrene.
The companies plan to spend about 10 billion yen to build a factory with an annual production capacity of 120,000 tonnes of polystyrene near Shanghai, it said.
